title: Musk Enters the Copilot Arena: Grok Bot Deeply Takes Over Microsoft Accounts

content_html:
Grok Bot has recently undergone a major upgrade and officially announced full integration with Microsoft accounts. Through dedicated plugins, it connects to core office components such as Outlook, Calendar, and OneDrive, enabling it to comprehensively assist users with complex daily office tasks, including sending and receiving emails, creating, modifying, and replying to meeting schedules, as well as browsing and uploading files to cloud storage.

Actually, the underlying connectors were already available back in May of this year. The key highlight of this update is adapting these connectors into a persistent cloud PC plugin for Grok Bot. This change marks a significant leap from Grok Bot's previous "passive response" mode, allowing it to actively handle work tasks, such as automatically reading emails and drafting replies in advance.

In terms of industry ecosystem and technical approach, major technology giants and open-source communities are actively developing intelligent agents based on Microsoft accounts. Currently, Microsoft Copilot, Anthropic, and open-source projects like OpenClaw are all competing in this space. Notably, Microsoft has adopted a relatively open standard licensing process for third parties, while Google has imposed more restrictions on automated login processes.

Compared to other similar products, the biggest advantage of Grok Bot is that users do not need to configure complex local devices or servers. After authorization, it can run continuously in the cloud 24/7. To ensure security and controllability, the system requires user approval before executing any critical operations, ensuring that the final decision-making power always remains with the user themselves.
